tasks.routeTitle: Differential forms and local Poincaré lemma with partitions of unity
tasks.currentSketch: Resolve the sheaf of locally constant functions by the de Rham complex, exact on stalks by the local Poincaré lemma. Fine sheaves are acyclic via partitions of unity, so global de Rham cohomology computes constant-sheaf cohomology, identified with singular cohomology on manifolds.

tasks.entryDescription: Differential forms and local Poincaré lemma with partitions of unity; Mayer–Vietoris induction; sheaf/cohomological resolution.
tasks.currentSketch: The de Rham complex is a fine resolution of the constant sheaf ℝ: local exactness is Poincaré lemma, and partitions of unity imply acyclicity. The resulting resolution theorem identifies its global-section cohomology with sheaf cohomology, hence singular cohomology. This is same method in sheaf language.

tasks.entryDescription: Radial homotopy operator; integrate along straight-line contraction; local cohomology/contractibility.
tasks.currentSketch: On a star-shaped domain with center a, define the homotopy operator on a k-form (k>0) by integrating contraction with the radial vector along H_t(x)=a+t(x−a), with the usual t^(k−1) factor. Differentiating H_t^*ω in t and integrating from 0 to 1 gives dKω+K(dω)=H_1^*ω−H_0^*ω. For closed k-forms with k>0, the right side is ω, so ω=d(Kω).

tasks.currentSketch: Contractibility implies reduced singular cohomology vanishes; via the de Rham theorem, closed positive-degree forms are exact. This is a consequence route that presupposes the de Rham theorem, and applies globally only when the domain is contractible.

tasks.entryDescription: Homotopy invariance of winding number; argument principle; perturbation estimate plus zero counting.
tasks.currentSketch: On boundary Γ, |g|<|f| implies f+t g never vanishes for t∈[0,1]. The winding number of f+tg around zero is homotopy-invariant, and argument principle equates winding number to number of zeros inside; f and f+g have equal counts.

tasks.entryDescription: Homotopy invariance of winding number; argument principle; perturbation estimate plus zero counting.
tasks.currentSketch: Apply the argument principle to f'/f and (f+g)'/(f+g); homotopy f+tg avoids zero on Γ, so the integer contour integral (1/2πi)∮(f+tg)'/(f+tg) is constant in t. Therefore zero counts agree.

tasks.entryDescription: Homotopy invariance of winding number; argument principle; perturbation estimate plus zero counting.
tasks.currentSketch: The strict boundary inequality ensures every f+tg stays nonzero on Γ. By Rouché's theorem's zero-count interpretation, a perturbation smaller than |f| cannot change the number of interior zeros. This is an application/reformulation, not proof; need winding-number argument.

tasks.routeTitle: Analytic continuation/nonvanishing of ζ on Re(s)=1
tasks.currentSketch: Set ψ(x)=∑_{n≤x}Λ(n). The explicit formula links ψ(x) to x plus sums over ζ zeros. Nonvanishing of ζ on Re(s)=1, plus zero-free-region bounds and a Tauberian passage, yields ψ(x)~x and hence π(x)~x/log x. Analytic continuation alone is insufficient.

tasks.entryDescription: Analytic continuation/nonvanishing of ζ on Re(s)=1; Tauberian theorem; elementary Selberg–Erdős proof. This is an example of distinct proof programs with different prerequisites, not a school-level entry.
tasks.currentSketch: Use the Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian theorem on F(s)=−ζ'(s)/ζ(s)=∑Λ(n)n^{-s}; a simple pole of F(s) at s=1 with residue 1 and no other singularity on Re(s)=1 implies ∑_{n≤x}Λ(n)~x, then partial summation yields PNT.

tasks.entryName: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
tasks.entryDescription: Dirichlet L-functions and Euler products; algebraic number fields/ideal classes in selected generalizations. State the full coprimality hypothesis and do not conflate proofs of special progressions with the theorem.
tasks.currentSketch: For (a,q)=1, expand L(s,χ)=∑χ(n)n^{-s}=∏_p(1−χ(p)p^{-s})^{-1}. A nonnegative product over characters and nonvanishing at s=1 show the character sum over primes in residue class a is asymptotic to 1/φ(q) of all primes; orthogonality isolates the class. Requires analytic nonvanishing of nonprincipal L(1,χ).

tasks.currentSketch: In K=Q(ζ_q), primes p≡a mod q have prescribed Frobenius element in Gal(K/Q). Chebotarev gives positive density conjugacy classes; in this abelian extension each element is a class, yielding infinitely many primes in each reduced residue class. This general theorem route is much deeper and assumes Chebotarev. A selected generalization uses class field theory/Chebotarev; it must retain (a,q)=1 for the classical theorem.

tasks.entryDescription: Laplace's method on the gamma integral; Wallis product plus factorial recurrences; Euler–Maclaurin summation; probabilistic/local central-limit arguments.
tasks.routeTitle: Laplace's method on the gamma integral
tasks.currentSketch: Use n!=∫_0^∞x^n e^{−x}dx. The exponent n log x−x has maximum at x=n; set x=n+√n u and Taylor-expand around the maximum. The rescaled integrand tends to e^{−u²/2}; tail bounds justify dominated convergence, giving √(2πn)n^n e^{−n}.

tasks.entryDescription: Laplace's method on the gamma integral; Wallis product plus factorial recurrences; Euler–Maclaurin summation; probabilistic/local central-limit arguments.
tasks.currentSketch: Wallis' product gives central binomial asymptotic binom(2n,n)~4^n/√(πn). Since binom(2n,n)=(2n)!/(n!)², factorial recurrences and a normalization limit yield Stirling's constant √(2π). Details require establishing the Wallis limit and recurrence ratio.

tasks.entryDescription: Laplace's method on the gamma integral; Wallis product plus factorial recurrences; Euler–Maclaurin summation; probabilistic/local central-limit arguments.
tasks.currentSketch: Euler–Maclaurin applied to log(n!)=∑_{k=1}^n log k gives (n+1/2)log n−n+C+o(1); evaluate C via Wallis product/integral as ½log(2π), yielding formula.

tasks.entryDescription: Baire-category proof; gliding-hump construction on Banach spaces; weak compactness/duality route in suitable formulations.
tasks.currentSketch: For p∈N set S_p={x: ||x||≤1 and ||T_nx||≤p for every n}. These are closed and cover the closed unit ball by pointwise boundedness. Baire gives some S_p containing a relative ball. Taking differences of points in that ball bounds ||T_nw|| uniformly for w in a neighborhood of 0; rescaling yields ||T_n||≤2p/δ for every n, hence sup_n||T_n||<∞.

tasks.currentSketch: Assume norms ||T_n|| unbounded; inductively choose unit vectors x_k with T_{n_k}x_k large while controlling earlier operators, and coefficients decreasing fast. A convergent series x=∑a_kx_k is constructed so ||T_{n_k}x||→∞, contradicting pointwise boundedness. The gliding-hump details require Banach completeness and careful subsequence selection.
